description.narrative:
The unprecedented outbreak of Coronavirus has already created a devastating social and humanitarian crisis within Sierra Leone, with severe negative economic impact, thus, reversing the impressive economic growth which the country had achieved in recent years. Since the outbreak of COVID-19, 782 people had been infected with the virus in Sierra Leone. (Source – MIC (SL 28/05/2020).
There are worrying signs that Sierra Leone is ill-equipped to contain the spread of the virus. Those in quarantine are often left without food or water supplies and disruptions to the agricultural, mining, construction, tourism and transportation sectors have had a severe knock on effect on people’s livelihoods and income security. Restrictions on movement of persons and the suspension of weekly community markets in rural areas (LOUMAs), has also resulted in food shortages in peri-urban communities. There are also fears that the same restrictions on movement and fear of infection have prevented farmers from going to work, putting an entire planting season at risk and making hunger a stark reality for already vulnerable, rural communities. The risk of malnutrition and starvation in the hardest hit areas makes urgent provision of food to vulnerable people and parish communities a top priority.
